title: Count-matrix construction and differential-expression results for pasilla

sources.locator: Input data > Count matrix input; About the pasilla dataset; Differential expression analysis; code chunks loadPasilla, reorderPasila, matrixInput, deseq, resOrder, sumRes
DESeq usage, arguments, model details, and examples

scientific_use: Align gene-by-sample raw counts with sample annotations, construct a DESeqDataSet with a condition design, estimate size factors, dispersions and negative-binomial GLMs using DESeq, and extract Wald-test log2 fold changes, p-values and adjusted p-values with results. The vignette demonstrates ordering/significance summaries and alpha-dependent independent filtering on Drosophila pasilla RNAi-treated versus untreated cell cultures.
tool_role_basis: The code composes DESeq2 constructors and analysis/result APIs on an existing count matrix; it does not implement the statistical methods.
inputs: Bundled pasilla_gene_counts.tsv.gz gene-by-sample count table and pasilla_sample_annotation.csv sample metadata; annotation rows require renaming fb-prefixed sample IDs and reordering to match count columns.
Condition is the DE variable; the example also carries sequencing type metadata, not used in this base design.
outputs: DESeqDataSet with fitted size factors, dispersions, coefficients and diagnostics.
DESeqResults table with log2FoldChange, standard error, statistic, pvalue and padj; summary and significant-gene subsets are shown.
dependencies: R/Bioconductor DESeq2 and its package dependencies; SummarizedExperiment/Bioconductor classes.
Input count matrix and sample table must have matching sample identifiers and order; no upstream quantification is performed in this unit.
evidence: Vignette states the study used Drosophila melanogaster cell cultures and RNAi knock-down of splicing factor pasilla, citing Brooks2010.
Bundled count and annotation filenames are loaded directly; annotation contains seven samples, condition, sequencing type, lane counts, total reads, and exon counts.
Vignette explicitly requires identical ordering of count columns and colData rows before construction.
DESeq manual documents the NB model and Wald/LRT interface; results page documents extracted statistics and independent filtering.
limitations: Source inspection only; no R code was executed and output values are not verified.
Raw FASTQ/alignment and count-generation provenance is deferred to the pasilla package vignette; this checkout contains only the count table and sample annotation.
The repository's LGPL license is code licensing evidence and does not establish redistribution rights for bundled biological data.

title: Adjust pasilla treatment comparison for sequencing type

sources.locator: Multi-factor designs; chunks multifactor, copyMultifactor, fixLevels, replaceDesign, multiResults, multiTypeResults

scientific_use: Refit the pasilla count data using ~ type + condition to control the treated-versus-untreated comparison for single-read versus paired-end sequencing type, then extract condition or type contrasts. This is a concrete confounding/adjustment analysis distinct from the base condition-only fit.
tool_role_basis: The workflow changes a DESeq2 design formula and invokes DESeq/results; it applies existing GLM functionality.
inputs: The pasilla DESeqDataSet and its condition and type sample annotations from the preceding count-matrix workflow; factor levels are normalized before fitting.
Same raw integer gene counts; no transformed counts are used for inference.
outputs: Refitted DESeqDataSet under ~ type + condition and results for condition by default or a specified type contrast.
dependencies: Requires the pasilla count-matrix construction and sample alignment in deseq2:vignette:pasilla-wald-analysis.
DESeq2; design must be full rank with adequate replication.
evidence: Vignette identifies condition as the variable of interest and type as sequencing protocol, then changes design to ~ type + condition and reruns DESeq.
Sample annotation source lists read layout for all seven samples, showing both single-read and paired-end types.
limitations: Only the documented worked design was inspected; no independent confounder diagnosis or numerical result was validated.
Dataset has small sample count and an imbalanced design context; author should inspect design rank and interpretability before task construction.

title: Import Salmon transcript quantifications and construct gene-level DESeqDataSet

sources.locator: Input data > Transcript abundance files and tximport/tximeta; chunks txiSetup, txiFiles, tximport, txi2dds

scientific_use: Read Salmon quant.sf files and a transcript-to-gene mapping with tximport, then create a gene-level DESeqDataSet with sample condition metadata. The source explains estimated counts and sample-specific offsets account for potential changes in average transcript length across samples; the result is ready for the standard DESeq analysis.
tool_role_basis: This is an import/composition workflow using tximport and DESeq2 constructors; it does not implement quantification or import algorithms.
inputs: Salmon quant.sf.gz files, sample table with run identifiers and condition, and tx2gene mapping; demonstration paths/data are supplied by the tximportData package.
Transcript quantification must already have been run; DESeq2 vignette recommends Salmon/kallisto/RSEM-like quantifiers upstream.
outputs: tximport object with gene-level estimated counts and abundance/length information, then DESeqDataSet created by DESeqDataSetFromTximport for downstream modeling.
dependencies: R packages tximport, tximportData, readr, DESeq2 and their dependencies.
Quantification files and transcript-to-gene mapping must correspond to the same reference and sample runs.
tximeta is described as a separate alternative import path with annotation metadata; it was not made a separate unit because the checked example is minimal and skipMeta=TRUE in its evaluated chunk.
evidence: The vignette names tximportData extdata files samples.txt, salmon/<run>/quant.sf.gz, and tx2gene.gencode.v27.csv and calls tximport(type='salmon', tx2gene=tx2gene).
The text says tximport uses estimated, not normalized, gene counts and provides offsets correcting potential changes in average transcript length.
Vignette states tximportData is demonstration-only; users supply their own quantification paths.
limitations: tximportData package files, sample table contents, dataset study identity, sizes and terms were not retrieved; record marks these unknown.
This unit ends at DESeqDataSet construction; quantifier execution and downstream DE results are outside this specific source section.
No data files were downloaded and no import was run.

title: Shrink pasilla log2 fold changes for ranking and visualization
source_kind: R Markdown vignette workflow and package manual

sources.locator: Differential expression analysis > Log fold change shrinkage for visualization and ranking; Alternative shrinkage estimators
Usage, arguments, value, details and examples

scientific_use: Take a fitted pasilla DESeqDataSet and coefficient, then estimate shrunken log2 fold changes for visualization and gene ranking. The vignette uses apeglm; manual examples compare apeglm, ashr and normal shrinkage estimators and documents threshold/s-value options.
tool_role_basis: The source applies DESeq2's lfcShrink and optional external shrinkage packages to fitted coefficients; no estimator implementation is created in the example.
inputs: A DESeqDataSet already processed by DESeq and a coefficient name from resultsNames(dds); example coefficient is condition_treated_vs_untreated.
For apeglm, coefficient selection is required; normal and ashr have distinct supported input semantics.
outputs: DESeqResults with shrunken log2FoldChange and posterior SD in lfcSE; optional s-values when requested.
dependencies: Depends on the fitted DESeqDataSet from the pasilla workflow.
apeglm or ashr package for those shrinkage types; DESeq2 supports normal internally.
evidence: Vignette says shrinkage is useful for visualization and ranking and demonstrates apeglm on the treated-versus-untreated coefficient.
Manual documents output estimate/uncertainty semantics and requirements for each shrinkage type.
limitations: Optional-package versions and shrinkage outputs were not tested.
Only pasilla's main coefficient is the worked example; interactions, threshold testing, and other shrinkage modes need author-specified choices.

title: Variance-stabilize counts for sample exploration and clustering
source_kind: package manual API and vignette sections

sources.locator: Data transformations and visualization > Count data transformations and variance stabilizing transformation

scientific_use: Transform normalized count data to approximately homoskedastic values for sample QA, PCA, clustering or other downstream machine learning. VST can be design-blind for unbiased sample comparisons or use the design for downstream work; fast vst deterministically selects a subset spanning mean normalized counts to estimate the dispersion trend.
tool_role_basis: The unit applies existing DESeq2 transformation APIs to count data; it does not implement a new transformation.
inputs: DESeqDataSet or count matrix; size factors and a dispersion-mean fit may be estimated as needed.
Parameters include blind and fitType; vst also uses nsub (default documented as 1000).
outputs: DESeqTransform or transformed normalized-count matrix, usable for sample distance/PCA/clustering; transformed values are not the inputs to DESeq differential testing.
dependencies: DESeq2; when a DESeqDataSet is supplied, compatible sample metadata/design are available for blind=FALSE.
For frozen transformation, save/reuse dispersionFunction from a prior dataset and apply with blind=FALSE.
evidence: Manual says VST aims for approximate homoskedasticity and is useful for outlier checking, visualization and clustering; describes blind behavior and frozen reuse.
Manual explicitly says DESeq testing uses raw counts, not VST/rlog values.
vst manual describes deterministic mean-spanning subset for faster trend estimation.
limitations: Examples use synthetic example datasets or generic inputs; no identifiable biological dataset is specified by the inspected manual.
No transformation was executed; downstream PCA suitability and residual mean-variance dependence are unverified.

title: Compare full and reduced negative-binomial GLMs with an LRT
scientific_use: For a replicated count experiment, fit nested full and reduced designs and test whether removing one or more terms significantly changes model deviance. Results include a test statistic and p-value for the joint removed terms; one displayed log2 fold change is not necessarily the only effect tested.
tool_role_basis: The documented operation applies the existing DESeq2 GLM fitting and likelihood-ratio test API to an existing DESeqDataSet.
inputs: DESeqDataSet with raw count assay and sample design; size factors/normalization factors and dispersion estimates must be available (manual example estimates them before nbinomLRT).
Full design matching design(object) and nested reduced formula or model matrix.
outputs: Updated DESeqDataSet with test results accessed through results; LRT compares full versus reduced model deviance.
dependencies: R/Bioconductor DESeq2; valid nested designs and sufficient replicate observations.
For glmGamPoi quasi-LRT, dispersions must first be estimated with glmGamPoi; this is a distinct option in manual.
evidence: nbinomLRT manual describes full/reduced inputs and chi-squared deviance test, gives example of estimating size factors/dispersions then testing reduced=~1.
DESeq manual describes LRT through test='LRT' and full/reduced design arguments.
Vignette FAQ explains LRT p-values test all terms/levels removed by reduced design while the result table displays one coefficient.
limitations: Manual example is generated synthetic data; no biological dataset is linked.
No LRT was run. The statistical interpretation depends on the selected full/reduced designs and their nesting.
Vignette-specific LRT use cases and extended interaction designs remain pending source-map leads.

title: Configure DESeq2 for single-cell count matrices
scientific_use: Apply the vignette's documented configuration guidance when using individual heterogeneous cells as samples: consider LRT, useT=TRUE, minmu=1e-6, disable automatic replicate outlier replacement, consider scran sum-factor size factors and glmGamPoi for speed/on-disk support, and distinguish this from within-cell-type pseudobulk comparisons across biological samples.
tool_role_basis: The source recommends composing existing DESeq2 and Bioconductor package options for analysis; it does not implement methods.
inputs: Single-cell gene count matrix with cells as columns and cell/sample metadata for design; the vignette provides recommendations rather than a dataset or complete executable analysis.
outputs: A configured DESeq2 analysis and differential test for a specified single-cell design; pseudobulk aggregation is an upstream alternative and is not implemented in this source section.
dependencies: DESeq2; optional scran for computeSumFactors, glmGamPoi for alternative fitting, zinbwave for zero-inflation modeling.
Sufficient design/replication and biological units must be considered; individual cells and biological replicates are not interchangeable.
evidence: Vignette explicitly distinguishes individual-cell heterogeneous mixture from pseudobulk aggregating cells and comparing within cell type across condition.
Vignette lists test='LRT', useT=TRUE, minmu=1e-6, minReplicatesForReplace=Inf, scran size factors, glmGamPoi and optional zinbwave.
limitations: This section is recommendations rather than a complete workflow and cites external benchmarks/papers that were not inspected.
No single-cell dataset or benchmark source is linked here; exact suitability of recommendations depends on study design and current package versions.
Do not treat cells as independent biological replicates without an explicit design rationale.

title: Replace count outliers using replicate-group trimmed means

sources.locator: replaceOutliers and replaceOutliersWithTrimmedMean usage, details and value

scientific_use: Identify extreme count observations using Cook's distances from a fitted DESeq2 model and optionally replace eligible counts with a replicate-group trimmed mean adjusted by sample normalization. Original counts are preserved in originalCounts, while replaced counts are available through counts().
tool_role_basis: This applies the package's documented outlier replacement operation to a fitted DESeqDataSet; no detection or replacement method is implemented in the source unit.
inputs: A DESeqDataSet already processed by DESeq, nbinomWaldTest or nbinomLRT with Cook's distances in assays(dds).
Replicated groups meeting minReplicates; parameters include trimmed fraction, Cook's cutoff and optional sample selection.
outputs: DESeqDataSet with replaced counts and original counts retained in assays(dds)[['originalCounts']]; Cook's distances are updated.
dependencies: DESeq2; fitted model, normalization factors/size factors and sample group metadata.
Replacement is automatically invoked within DESeq for eligible groups; explicit calls may be appropriate for controlled workflows.
evidence: Manual documents Cook's-distance-based selection, trimmed-mean replacement, preserved originals, minimum replicate eligibility, and that DESeq calls this internally.
DESeq manual says default replacement eligibility starts at seven replicates and replacement is disabled for glmGamPoi.
limitations: No dataset or output was inspected or executed; the seven-sample pasilla example has groups below the documented default replacement threshold.
Continuous covariates and small replicate groups limit applicability; authors must choose whether to expose automated or explicit replacement behavior.
